title: 'Hunkkaar' Trailer: Aneet Padda's Student Accuses Powerful Godman of Abuse
excerpt: The JioHotstar series, streaming September 25, casts Aneet Padda as a 17-year-old who accuses a revered godman of abuse — with Fatima Sana Shaikh as the cop investigating the case.
body:
• JioHotstar has released the full trailer of Hunkkaar: The Roar, premiering September 25, 2026 on the streamer.
  • Aneet Padda plays Meenu Rawat, a 17-year-old student who, according to the trailer, accuses the revered cult leader "Baapji" of sexually abusing her.
  • Fatima Sana Shaikh plays ACP Jasleen Singh Soni, the police officer leading the investigation; the ensemble includes Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub, Arjun Mathur, Ram Kapoor, Raghubir Yadav and Rajesh Sharma.
  • The series was filmed before Padda's breakout in Saiyaara (2025) and is executive-produced by Priyanka Chopra Jonas through Purple Pebble Pictures.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=k_P_O1zAVug

A Trailer About One Accusation — and Everything That Follows

The official trailer of Hunkkaar: The Roar dropped this week, and it centers on a single, incendiary allegation. In the trailer, Padda's character, 17-year-old Meenu Rawat, walks into a police station with her mother and reports that Baapji — the spiritual leader who runs her school and commands a devoted following — violated and assaulted her. What begins as one complaint, according to the makers, sets in motion a high-stakes investigation that becomes a national reckoning.

The trailer presents the story as three parallel battles over the same truth: on the ground, Fatima Sana Shaikh plays ACP Jasleen Singh Soni, the gritty police officer assigned to uncover what happened; in the courtroom, an underdog lawyer named Bhalerao takes up the matter; and in the media, a determined journalist tracks the developments as public opinion grows almost as influential as the investigation itself. With Baapji's influence reaching into politics and the administration, the trailer shows the young accuser increasingly cornered, with the people around her questioning whether she is as "innocent" as she claims to be.

Context & Background

Hunkkaar: The Roar is created by Karan D Kapadia and Nitya Mehra, directed by Kapadia, Mehra and Heeraz Marfatia, and produced by Birla Studios and Applause Entertainment in association with Purple Pebble Pictures — a Mangata Films production with Priyanka Chopra Jonas as executive producer. The teaser, released September 1, had already revealed the premise: Meenu Rawat, a student at Mahasherni School located within Baapji's Shaburi Fort, levels the accusation that drives the plot.

The series has an unusual backstory. Padda shot it before her Bollywood debut in Mohit Suri's romantic blockbuster Saiyaara (2025), which catapulted her and co-star Ahaan Panday to stardom. According to industry sources cited by Bollywood Hungama, the project was completed well before that breakout but held back strategically — studios waited until Padda's box-office clout surged, turning a shelved series into a commercially viable event release. Padda herself has owned that history: "Presenting a little something I shot before Saiyaara," she wrote on Instagram. "Nahi hoga insaaf ka intezaar, bas goonjegi sachhai ki Hunkkaar."

"She is young, complicated and not always easy to understand, that's what makes her real. Her one constant? A refusal to be silenced. I hope audiences see her vulnerability and the defiance at the heart of her journey."

— Aneet Padda, on playing Meenu Rawat

Impact & Analysis

The trailer positions Hunkkaar squarely in the tradition of social thrillers that put the survivor at the center rather than using her as a plot device. The premise — a teenage girl accusing a powerful, politically connected godman — draws on a fault line Indian audiences know well: the series examines how difficult it can be to establish the truth when the accused wields faith, money and political cover.

"As a producer, I've always wanted to stand behind stories that have something to say, and 'Hunkkaar: The Roar' is very much that. I hope the story stays with audiences the way it stayed with me."

— Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Executive Producer

Diaspora Angle

Diaspora audiences will encounter Hunkkaar on two levels. The first is the JioHotstar pipeline itself: the streamer's global reach means a series about justice, institutional power and media trials premieres simultaneously for viewers in India and abroad. The second is Padda's arc — from an unknown who shot this series in obscurity to a breakout star returning to it with leverage — a career story that mirrors the industry's new OTT-era mobility. For NRIs tracking which Hindi stories travel, a courtroom drama about faith, power and a young woman's refusal to be silenced is exactly the kind of socially anchored series that finds a global audience.

What's Next

Hunkkaar: The Roar premieres September 25, 2026, exclusively on JioHotstar. With the trailer launch complete and the cast — including Fatima Sana Shaikh, last seen in Gustaakh Ishq (2025) — beginning promotions, the coming weeks will test whether the series' sober, procedural take on its subject can cut through the crowded OTT slate. For Padda, it is also a career checkpoint: her first release since Saiyaara, and the first evidence of whether her screen persona extends beyond romance.
